text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Wednesday:

- A security guard at Union Bank of Switzerland found historical files that were to be shredded despite a federal law banning destruction of files. He gave them to the Israeli Community in Zurich. UBS issued a statement saying it regretted its "mistake".
- Prodega Group posted a 4.6 percent rise in sales to 923 million Swiss francs for 1996.
- Stratec Group , a firm specialised in medical technology, registered a 21.7 percent sales increase to 224.6 million Swiss francs in 1996.
- Swiss Foreign Minister Flavio Cotti meets with Italy's Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini in Rome to discuss relations between Berne and the European Union.
- Nearly 200,000 customers left Helsana Health Insurance in 1996, mainly due to its 6.5 percent rise in premiums for 1997.
The company said it will cut some 200 jobs this year.
- Retail group Usego Hofer Curti AG posted a 5.9 percent increase in consolidated sales to two billion Swiss francs in 1996.
- Siemens Schweiz AG posted a 2.4 percent decline in sales in the 1995/96 fiscal year ended September. Despite the decline, net profit rose to 32.5 million Swiss francs.
- The 1997 Louis-Jeantet Prize for Medicine was awarded to three British scientists for their work in cancer research. The prize of 1.8 million Swiss francs goes towards continued research.
